$comment: RLTP's two-way-scan ceremony expressed in the ToIP DTGWG ceremony-definition format (informative interop artifact). The normative definition is spec/encounter-layer.md 5.8; this file exists so DTGWG tooling can read the RLTP ceremony, and to concretely instantiate the loosely described derivation of the registry's mutual-attestation/0.1.
title: RLTP two-way scan (offline mutual encounter)
summary: Both parties display and scan each other's contact cards, each confirms recognition, and each issues the other an encounter credential. No third party, no ordering, no network during the enactment; credentials may move long afterwards.

first-person.description: One of the two people present; the name distinguishes, it does not order.

attest-first.description: Delivers the encounter credential this party issues about the other, binding the other's fresh challenge. Anchor-rooted; simultaneous with attest-second.

anchor.derivation: The RLTP enactment binding (Encounter Layer 5.4): a multibase-encoded multihash over the JCS canonicalization of {ceremony, challenges}, where the challenges are the two fresh single-use values (>=128 bits each) from the two exchanged contact cards -- material neither party could have produced alone. This concretely instantiates the derivation the DTGWG registry's mutual-attestation/0.1 describes loosely.

sideEffects.rationale: Each party mints an immutable, never-revoked encounter credential about the other.

exposure.rationale: Each step delivers credential material the other party retains. enactmentPrivacy is plain, deliberately: under RLTP's stable anchors the credential pair is correlatable from the anchors alone, so blinding the enactment identifier would claim a privacy property the anchors do not support. RLTP states this honestly (Encounter Layer, Privacy Considerations).
